item.description:
Changed

  • Each Settings page has its own colored icon in the sidebar, like System Settings.

Added

  • A "Team reviews" example tab, and a Review option for pull requests requested from one of your teams, picked from the teams GitHub says you're on. The Review menu also tells "me or my teams" apart from "me only".
  • On a Mac without a notch, Pullo now shows a small tab at the top of the screen, so you can find it and hover it. CI progress shows on it too.
  • Opening Pullo again from Finder or Spotlight opens the panel.
  • While you set up, copy the gh auth login command or open Terminal right from the panel. Pullo adds your account as soon as you log in.
  • ⌘, in the panel opens Settings.
  • Choose which display Pullo shows on: the built-in one, the main one, or the one with the pointer (Settings → General).
  • Pick another shortcut to open the panel, or turn it off (Settings → Shortcuts), handy since ⌥⌘P is also Finder's Show Path Bar. Pullo tells you when another app already uses the shortcut.
  • Pullo can hold alerts while an app is full screen and show one summary when you leave, like during Focus (Settings → Alerts). It's off by default.
  • The Actions list works from the keyboard: ↑↓ pick a run, ↩ opens it, ↩ again opens it on GitHub and esc goes back.
  • VoiceOver reads alerts and confirmations out loud as they appear, tells which pull request tab is selected and how many PRs it has, and can show a PR's failed checks.

Changed

  • The panel stays open while you set up your first account, even when you switch to Terminal. "Not now" closes it.
  • When the panel opens under the pointer, the arrow keys, Return and Esc work right away.
  • The welcome alert mentions the ⌥⌘P shortcut.
  • Pullo uses less battery and network. It stops checking GitHub while your Mac is asleep, its screen is off or locked, or it's offline, and checks once as soon as you're back. With the panel closed, the Actions side only keeps a close eye on runs you started.

Fixed

  • When adding an account fails, Pullo says what went wrong in plain words and offers a way to fix it.
  • When GitHub's request limit is reached, Pullo waits until it resets instead of asking again every minute. When GitHub keeps failing, it waits a bit longer each time, up to five minutes, and when your sign-in is rejected it stops asking until you try again.
  • Pullo now finds gh installed with MacPorts, Nix, mise or anywhere on your shell's PATH, and reads gh's settings from XDG_CONFIG_HOME when you use it.
  • A slow or broken gh no longer holds Pullo up, and Pullo stops asking it for a token on every refresh after it fails. "Check again" in Settings → Accounts asks right away.
  • After GitHub was slow once, Pullo kept asking for shorter lists until you quit it. It now goes back to the full lists after half an hour, and a slow connection on your side no longer counts.
  • Repositories your organization blocks with single sign-on no longer slow down the Actions side.
  • Removing an account while Pullo was refreshing could bring its pull requests and runs back.
  • Re-running or cancelling a run while the Actions list was refreshing now shows the new state right away instead of on the next check.
  • If Pullo can't read some of your saved tabs, for example after using an older version, it keeps the ones it can read instead of replacing them all, and keeps a copy of the rest.
  • A pull request that briefly drops out of GitHub's results no longer alerts you again about the same review request or forgets what you've already read.
  • Fixed a crash when GitHub listed the same pull request twice.
  • Pullo no longer uses more and more memory the longer it runs.
  • When gh's token is revoked, the Actions side now picks up the new one once you sign in again, like the pull request side does.
  • With Reduce Motion on, the panel fades instead of bouncing, and the loading screen and lists no longer slide, blur or shimmer.
  • With Increase Contrast on, dimmed text in the panel is brighter and easier to read. Section titles in Actions and the keyboard hints are a little easier to read too.
  • Time units like "5m" and "2h" now follow the app's language, and a message in Settings → Accounts is now translated.

Security

  • Links from checks only open web pages (http and https), so a check can't point Pullo at a file or another app.

Removed

  • Pullo no longer counts how many Macs check for updates. It checks GitHub for updates again, like before 0.10.1, and nothing about your Mac is kept anywhere.

item.title: 0.8.0-beta.5
item.description:
Added

  • A new Actions side in the panel shows your GitHub Actions runs: what's running, waiting for approval or just finished, with job progress. Switch to it with the pill under the open notch, or ⌘← and ⌘→. It looks at the repositories you pushed to recently and the ones with your open pull requests, and filters by Mine, Everyone or Deploys.
  • Click a run in Actions to see its jobs, with failures first, matrix jobs grouped and the step that failed. From there you can re-run the failed jobs, cancel a run that's still going (click twice to confirm) or open it on GitHub. Esc goes back to the list.
  • Make your own tabs for the Actions side in Settings → Tabs, per account: pick who started the run, the repository, part of the workflow name, the branch (release/* matches the start), the event and the status. Mine, Everyone and Deploys become regular tabs you can edit, reorder or remove, and there are ready-made ones like Production deploys or Failing on main. The slider button next to the tabs opens the settings.
  • The run detail lists every step of each job, like GitHub does, with its status and how long it took. The job that's running or failed opens by itself, the others open with a click, and clicking a step opens its log on GitHub right at that step.

Changed

  • The closed notch now also shows workflow runs you started, like a deploy, with the workflow's name. The ring turns red as soon as a job fails, and the notch flashes the result when the run finishes.
  • With the Glass panel style, the tabs, filters, account, search, buttons, the Pull requests / Actions pill and the toasts use macOS Liquid Glass and react to the pointer, instead of flat shapes drawn by the app. The Solid style looks the same as before.

Fixed

  • The pill under the open notch follows the panel style, so it's glass when the panel is, instead of always black.
  • Tooltips show up next to the pointer, under the thing you hover (or above it when there's no room), and always inside the panel. Before, some were cut off by the panel edge, hidden behind other parts of the list, or showed up on the wrong side.
  • The count on a tab with unread pull requests stays white like the others, with a small blue dot, instead of turning the whole number blue.

• Merge pull request #1 from jordan-cod/release/0.3.0
  • Let the repo reference give way before the event in stacked alerts
  • Manage accounts only in Settings
  • Put a face on alerts, and alert when your PR is merged or closed
  • Turn Settings into a sidebar window with six pages
  • Spin the refresh icon on its own center, starting upright
  • Use an open envelope for mark as read
  • Open hover hints beside their view, above the title
  • Explain icons with an in-panel hover hint
  • One Linear-style status icon per row, everything else gray
  • Plain status tags, a quieter age, and logins without the company suffix
  • Show the filter as a field instead of a header icon
  • List stacked alerts line by line, most important first
  • Quiet the panel down
  • Raise text contrast and put a glyph in the CI dot
  • Match the row age to the list order, and make #N search exact
  • Don't mark your own new PRs unread, and confirm account removal
  • Alert on every new reviewer and say who commented
• Ship a signed, notarized disk image for downloads

• Give notarization two hours, enough for a new account's first review
  • Number builds by commit count so they always grow
  • Move to actions/checkout v7, off the deprecated Node 20
  • Ship updates with Sparkle and release from CI
  • Hold an alert while the pointer is over it
  • Play a sound on new alerts
  • Only take clicks over the visible part of the notch
  • Keep the notch on the built-in screen
  • Add an app icon
  • Remove build and demo scripts
  • README: cover external displays and drop the Gatekeeper note
  • Show the notch on external displays
  • Initial commit
